scope: SOURCE/CONTRACT review of repository UI, API, services and guides; not live qualification, rollout evidence or a claim that every feature is enabled in production. This provenance stays outside indexed guides. Upload and packaging require whole-pack review.

claims: Platform owns deployment configuration and releases; Engage is a connected embedded or standalone experience; Desk provides enabled deployment-scoped human support and separately authorized reviews.
Customer onboarding distinguishes identity, workspace creation, linking, template enrollment and later deployment; workspace creation alone does not deploy or incur AI use.
Customer navigation grows with resources; knowledge and connection views select a deployment and target release, and Human support depends on configured capability.
Templates bootstrap editable settings; Configuration and Advanced are view depth, not additional staff authority.
Draft, publication, deployment verification, app readiness and observed answer quality are distinct evidence.
limitations: No universal template, provider, Desk, review or support-workspace availability is claimed.
Current execution context records production support as not launched; the document directs customers only to the support channel available to their account.
No price, SLA, retention, residency or future product promise is introduced.

claims: Native Supabase customer identity is separate from active Console membership; existing accounts are not claimed by verified email alone.
New users explicitly create a workspace when eligible; existing-account linking requires both the local customer session and verified Supabase identity.
Registration sends an email-verification instruction, and password recovery uses the recovery email session, matching new passwords and subsequent sign-in.
Login fields start empty; customer Advanced view does not change the account role, and team management is conditional.
Desk assignment and Engage visitor authentication are distinct from Console customer administration; local sign-out must not be described as immediate revocation of every issued integration token.
limitations: Email delivery, external provider uptime and a particular customer's membership are not verified by this source review.
No universal social login, MFA, invitation flow, automatic account reassignment or immediate downstream token revocation is claimed.
Registration and available templates may be disabled independently of existing-account access.

claims: The same shared versioning flow supports editable drafts, validation, immutable published versions, explicit target and compatible artifact selection, apply and release verification.
Templates and offers are bootstrap defaults rather than permanent restrictions; ordinary existing-production upgrades do not inherently require new apps, manual upgrade approval or staging promotion.
Guided staging-to-production promotion retains explicit verification and assignment activation; publishing is not app reassignment or data transfer.
Reset to template changes the draft only, preserves installed plugins, credentials, bindings and identity, and does not publish, deploy or recover data.
Release verification is exact-release evidence and does not guarantee all knowledge freshness or semantic answer quality.
limitations: Permissions, required credentials, artifact compatibility and actual verification remain mandatory; no authorization bypass is suggested.
Historical restrictions in older implementation guides are not treated as the current lifetime-upgrade contract.
No zero-downtime, automatic conversation migration, automatic index transfer or universal rollback guarantee is claimed.

claims: Plugin types contribute configuration and capabilities; install changes compile into a draft and need publication and apply before affecting the runtime.
The generated install form and approved-connection workflow separate nonsecret configuration, endpoint/account approval and write-only credentials.
Reviewed connection bindings are specific to a version, target and slot, and local credential status is not provider-health evidence.
Connections displays source state, freshness, last success and counts scoped to the selected target release.
Platform revocation is distinct from external provider key revocation and stopping an already running credential consumer.
limitations: Approved connections is conditional on the installed capability and profile; the document does not promise arbitrary URL or credential setup in every workspace.
No business account creation, source system ownership, universal provider support or automatic production authorization is claimed.
No live provider authentication, synchronization latency or upstream availability is certified by this document.

claims: Embedded and standalone are separate installation delivery modes that can share one deployment; the UI offers creating the complementary delivery from an existing app configuration.
Connect deployment derives its proposed target/release from deployment context and existing assignment, while allowing explicit changes and draft-only configuration before verified activation.
Appearance fields and the synthetic preview cover names, public HTTPS logo, colour, appearance, welcome/input text and configurable sample views without AI calls or real actions.
The exact installer script is generated by Console, uses a public installation identifier, belongs once in the site layout and requires exact allowed origins plus an active ready installation.
Standalone delivery resolves the installation by origin, direct-runtime traffic reaches the assigned deployment, and reviewed private profiles retain their trusted adapter path.
limitations: Two delivery installations are not promised automatic ongoing synchronization of all appearance edits or shared visitor sessions.
The preview is synthetic and cannot qualify arbitrary custom renderer code, live sign-in, actions, answer quality or handover.
Capabilities and profiles must actually be installed and configured; a visible control grants no backend permission.
Reassignment is not claimed to migrate a live conversation, and editing an active installation follows its existing disable requirement.

claims: Custom domains identify standalone installations on the shared frontend, not new AI runtimes or customer business databases.
Console emits app-specific TXT ownership and configured CNAME routing instructions; explicit Verify begins ownership, applied-route and exact-host HTTPS checks.
The configured background worker continues ROUTING_PENDING verification after explicit intent; initial ownership failure still requires correction and another verification request.

Required runtime origin/identity changes are reviewed and published/applied through the existing deployment lifecycle, including visible unrelated draft changes and explicit use of the verified update.
External identity-provider redirect configuration may remain manual; app readiness and explicit activation are separate from domain verification.
limitations: SOURCE/CONTRACT only: this review does not establish that any new customer domain, shared routing setting, DNS record or certificate is currently ready.
No fixed DNS propagation time, certificate timing, automatic identity-provider mutation or root-domain/alternative DNS-record support is promised.
The CNAME is the routing instruction; verification also relies on applied route ownership and direct healthy HTTPS, not merely a matching DNS label.
A domain check does not guarantee authentication, runtime query success, upstream business access or semantic answer quality.
